key_insight: lPINN moves most of the learning offline by pretraining nonlinear basis functions, then solves new PDE instances online with only a frozen linear layer and physics-based optimization.
engineering_relevance: This can cut inference cost dramatically while improving accuracy for forward and inverse PDE problems, making PINN-style solvers more practical for repeated or real-time engineering use.
method: Learn continuous neural basis functions from an ensemble of numerical solutions in an offline stage.
Pretrain the basis using solution data plus derivative information or physics residuals.
For each new problem, freeze the basis and optimize only the final linear coefficients against PDE residuals and any IC/BC, regularization, or observation terms.
evidence_signal: The paper reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors and online speedups from about 10x to over 1000x versus vanilla PINNs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the offline training ensemble, so the learned basis may generalize less well if the target PDE regime differs substantially from the pretraining data.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
